symptom: ako/mxcli#2096 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1797): `call microflow Lab.Target (Qty = '5')` against an Integer parameter passes `mxcli check -p` and exec, then mx check 11.14.0 fails CE0117 "Error(s) in expression" at the call activity; likewise another enumeration, Boolean for DateTime, Decimal for Integer, a primitive for an object parameter, and a bare word
cause: slot_resolver.go declared `CallArgument.Value` with ResolveBy "TargetParameter", but nothing resolved it and checkSlotKind skips every ResolveBy slot; E013 (bare word) was scoped to create/change members; and a flow the script itself creates had no parameter types in the catalog reader
file: `mdl/exprcheck/call_argument.go` (CallArgumentSlot, checkCallArgumentKind, callArgAccepted), `mdl/exprcheck/adapters/check.go` (qualified slot), `mdl/exprcheck/parser.go` (E013 prefix), `mdl/exprcatalog/exprcatalog.go` (mfParamRef, DeclareFlow, KnowsEntity), `mdl/executor/typecheck.go` (scriptFlowParams), test `mdl/executor/typecheck_call_argument_2096_test.go`, `mdl-examples/bug-tests/2096-call-argument-parameter-type.mdl`
insight: A ResolveBy entry in the expectations table is a TODO, not a rule: grep for who resolves it before trusting it (only AttributeOf:Parent had a resolver, by qualifying the slot path). Resolve TargetParameter the same way, qualifying the slot with flow(param), rather than writing a second resolver. Measure the whole matrix in ONE project with `mx check -j`: 9 parameter types x 19 argument shapes as one caller microflow each gives the predicate in a 17s run, and diffing it against `check -p` gave 133 caught / 0 false / 8 deliberate misses. The matrix surprised twice: `empty` into a BOOLEAN parameter is CE0117 (into every other type it builds), left unreported pending its own cross-version measurement; and [%CurrentDateTime%] must be typed DateTime (argKind), since inferKind calls every token a String and would refuse it for a DateTime parameter. Plausible wrong turn: trusting the kind scope for enumeration variables. In a microflow SIGNATURE `enum M.E` does not set ExplicitEnum (visitor_microflow.go), so the parameter sits in the entity scope and infers as Object; settle it by asking the catalog whether the name is an enumeration (document names are unique per module). Object-vs-list and entity identity stay silent: the entity scope cannot tell a list variable from an object. Still open: exec's preflight does not run TypeCheckProgram at all, so this rule, like every E0xx rule, fails `check -p` but does not stop `exec`.
